description: Maya has four reserved seats for a sold-out family theater performance and must decide who will use them, how the seats will be assigned, and what accompaniment plan to make, with input from her brother Jordan and cousin Leah.

shared_context.S1: Maya has four reserved seats for a sold-out theater performance on Saturday evening.
shared_context.S2: The four seats are in the same section: one aisle seat in row B and three ordinary seats in row C.
shared_context.S3: Maya decides who uses the tickets and how the seats are assigned.
shared_context.S4: Before Maya finalizes the ticket plan, the family routinely goes around the room so each person can mention anything that should affect the arrangement.
shared_context.S5: The theater requires any guest under age sixteen to attend with an adult ticket holder.
shared_context.S6: Maya plans to attend the performance herself and use one of the four tickets.

PF1.text: Jordan is using crutches after ankle surgery and cannot manage the stairs to row C; he needs the row-B aisle seat to attend comfortably.

PF2.text: Leah promised her thirteen-year-old son Eli that he could use one of the tickets, and Eli may attend only if Leah accompanies him.

acceptance_conditions: The four tickets must be assigned exactly to Maya, Jordan, Leah, and Eli, with Leah accompanying Eli.
The accessible row-B aisle seat must be assigned to Jordan.
Leah's promise to Eli and need to accompany him must be reflected in the ticket-holder decisions or cited in the settlement justification.
A commitment may confirm that Leah accompanies Eli into the performance.
A commitment may confirm that the remaining three named people use the row-C seats.

decisive_facts.why: Jordan's crutches and inability to use row C change both the seat map and the accessible-seat field by requiring Jordan to receive the row-B aisle seat.
Leah's promise to Eli changes the row-C ticket holders from the adults alone to Maya, Leah, and Eli, and changes the plan by requiring Leah to accompany Eli.
